- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates or lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% and add 1–2 day lag correction.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use mean-reversion anchor.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign horizon; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast trajectory.
- When true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often holds high values; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until reversion signal is confirmed.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.5), model often overfits short-term noise; apply 3-day smoothing filter to forecast before output.
